blocks.text: The reality of supply chain forecasting in Excel

Excel is the tool you trust for complex supply chain forecasting. You build models that track inventory levels, lead times, and demand spikes. Yet, the data you need lives in many places. You pull files from ERP systems like SAP or Oracle. You download CSV files from supplier portals. You copy and paste data from emails. Each manual step introduces a risk of error. Your goal is to move from data entry to actual insight as quickly as possible.

Data reconciliation is often the biggest bottleneck in your day. You spend hours aligning data between your ERP, carrier systems, and internal spreadsheets. To do this faster, use Excel features that automate the heavy lifting. Power Query is your best friend on Mac. Use Data > Get Data to connect directly to your sources. This avoids the manual copy and paste process entirely. Once you build a connection, you can refresh your data with a single click.
When your data is messy, use the TRIM and CLEAN functions in Excel to remove hidden spaces and non-printable characters. This prevents lookup errors in your forecasting models.
blocks.title: Clean your data first

blocks.text: You spend a large part of your week triaging emails from suppliers and internal stakeholders. This constant switching between Excel and Outlook breaks your focus. Research shows it takes over 23 minutes to get back into a deep state of concentration. Try to batch your email time. Check your inbox at set times rather than reacting to every notification. Use folders and rules in Outlook to prioritize urgent messages from key suppliers.

Lazur sees your screen and answers out loud. It does not click buttons for you, but it guides you to the right menu or formula. It keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on your data.

blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for supply chain analysis

Your Mac is a powerful machine for data analysis. Ensure your apps are updated to the latest versions for the best performance. If you work with large datasets, keep your Excel files on a local drive rather than a network share. This reduces latency when you perform complex calculations. Use shortcuts like ⌘ ⌥ V to paste values only, which keeps your spreadsheets lightweight. Always verify your data sources before you start a new forecast model.
Next steps for your forecasting workflow

Look at the time you spend on repetitive tasks. Can you automate any part of your data cleaning? Could a template reduce the time you spend on status reports? Start small. Improve one part of your process each week. If you need help finding a specific feature in Excel, ask Lazur to point it out. Focus on the work that adds real value to your supply chain strategy.

faq.question: How can I speed up Excel on my Mac?
faq.answer: Keep your files local, limit the use of volatile functions like OFFSET or INDIRECT, and use Power Query to handle large data imports instead of manual pasting.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with my company's ERP system?
faq.answer: Lazur works with any web-based ERP system that runs in your browser. It sees your screen and can guide you through the interface just like any other app.

faq.question: Is my data safe when I use Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur only sees your screen and hears your voice while you hold the shortcut keys. The information is sent to AI providers to answer your request and is not stored or used to train models.
